title: Aurum Alpha RBAC model
description: The shapes of standards/rbac.md: permission, scope, role and grant. This file fixes the model; contracts/rbac/decisions.json fixes the behaviour. schemaVersion 1 — evolves additively per PC6.

permission.description: resource.action, lowercase, snake_case within segments, exactly two segments (RB2). The dot is reserved for permissions and the colon for scopes so no identifier is ambiguous. Three segments are forbidden: system.dashboard.view is system_dashboard.view, which keeps the check an equality rather than a prefix question.

scope.description: Either the literal 'global' or a type:id pair such as tenant:acme (RB5). The application declares which scope types exist and how they contain one another; this contract fixes the shape and leaves the hierarchy to the application, because a standard naming the levels would fit no two products.

role.description: A named set of permissions (RB3). Roles do not nest and do not inherit — a role that should have what another has lists the same permissions, so that what a person can do stays readable from the role's own definition.

name.description: Stable identifier. Display names are the application's own concern.

permissions.description: Every entry MUST be in the application's declared permission set (RB1), validated at write time. A stored role carrying a typo grants nothing and says nothing.

grant.description: Binds a subject to a role within a scope (RB5). Grants are additive and there are no negative grants: a subject's permissions at a scope are the union of every grant that applies there.

subject.description: The application's own user or service-account id, per IP1. Never the identity provider's subject.

decision.description: What check() returns (RB8). Never a bare boolean: a denial that cannot say why is the SC2 reason-giving failure on the surface where it matters most. The reason is logged and shown to an administrator; it never reaches an unauthorised caller, whose response is the HA3 envelope.

reason.description: Which grant satisfied the check. Absent when allowed is false — there is no satisfying grant to name, and 'no grant applies' is the whole reason.
